/-!
# Erdős Problem 412

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/412](https://www.erdosproblems.com/412)

Reviewed by @b-mehta on 2025-05-27
-/

open ArithmeticFunction.sigma

namespace Erdos412

/--
Let $σ_1(n)=σ(n)$, the sum of divisors function, and $σ_k(n) = σ(σ_{k-1}(n))$.
Is it true that, for every $m, n ≥ 2$, there exist some $i, j$ such that $σ_i(m) = σ_j(n)$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_412 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (m ≥ 2) (n ≥ 2), ∃ i j, (σ 1)^[i] m = (σ 1)^[j] n := by
  sorry

end Erdos412

reformulations.difference: The source introduces the iterated sequence starting at σ₁(n)=σ(n), whereas Lean permits natural iteration counts i,j including zero.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For any function f, a meeting f^[i](m)=f^[j](n) yields a meeting at positive indices i+1,j+1 by applying f to both sides. Conversely, positive indices are natural indices. Thus permitting zero iterations does not change the existential meeting condition, or its universal quantification over m,n≥2. This equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean as source_statement_equivalence.
